title: Fabada Asturiana
subtitle: Spanish white bean stew with chorizo and morcilla
excerpt: The great bean stew of Asturias in northern Spain: large white fabes beans simmered slowly with chorizo, morcilla, and cured pork shoulder until the broth is rich and silky and the beans are creamy and whole. One of the most important stews of Spanish cuisine.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fabada asturiana is the defining dish of the Asturias region of northern Spain, a mountainous region known for its cattle, its cider, and its bean stew. The fabe asturiana is a specific large white bean variety grown in Asturias, with a notably creamy texture and thin skin; they are available dried from Spanish delicatessens. Cannellini beans are a reasonable substitute. The compango is the collective name for the three meats that accompany the beans: chorizo (the Spanish cured sausage), morcilla asturiana (the blood sausage of the region), and lacón (cured pork shoulder). The stew is never rushed: the beans must absorb the fat and paprika from the sausages over a long, gentle simmer, and the broth should be glossy and thick without any flour. The technique of susto (fright), adding a small amount of cold water to the pot periodically to slow the boil and keep the beans whole, is a traditional technique that prevents the skins from splitting.

content.text: Never let the stew boil hard; it should simmer so gently the surface barely trembles. Vigorous boiling breaks the bean skins. Add a splash of cold water (susto) if the stew begins to boil too quickly. The beans are ready when completely tender and the broth is silky from the fat rendered from the sausages. Reheat gently the next day; fabada is almost always better on day two.

items.preparation: dried; soaked in cold water overnight; or fabe asturiana if available
cooking chorizo, whole or in large pieces
adds smokiness in place of morcilla if unavailable
cured (lacón) or smoked pork shoulder; or smoked back bacon in a piece

content.text: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a large pot. Cover with cold water by 6 cm. Bring to the boil and cook for 5 minutes; drain. Return the beans to the pot. Add the chorizo, pork shoulder, whole onion, whole garlic cloves, bay leaves, paprika, saffron with its soaking water, and olive oil. Cover with fresh cold water by 4 cm.

Bring slowly to the boil, then reduce to the gentlest possible simmer. Cook uncovered for 1 hour 30 minutes, adding small splashes of cold water whenever the stew begins to boil too hard. The beans should remain submerged throughout.

Continue to simmer very gently for a further 30 minutes until the beans are completely tender and creamy and the broth is silky and opaque. Season with salt. Remove the whole onion and garlic cloves. Slice the meats. Serve the beans in deep bowls with the sliced meats alongside and crusty bread.
